newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus issues murder warrants for north officials.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus issues murder warrants for north officials.

text.p: Cyprus on Wednesday issued arrest warrants for five prominent Turkish and Turkish Cypriot officials on suspicion they murdered a young Greek Cypriot during protests along a U.N.-manned buffer zone in August.
"The arrest warrants will be given to Interpol," Cypriot Attorney-general Alecos Markides told a news conference.

The five are the agriculture minister of the breakaway Turkish Cypriot state, the former commander of Turkish forces in northern Cyprus, the head of Turkish Cypriot security forces, the commander of a Turkish army battalion and the chief of Turkish Cypriot police.
Markides said all are wanted on suspicion of killing Greek Cypriot Solomos Solomos on August 14.
Solomos, 26, was shot dead as he climbed a pole to tear down a Turkish flag at the edge of the United Nations controlled buffer zone dividing the island in the south eastern village of Dherinia.
His death came three days after that of another Greek Cypriot, Tasos Issac, who was beaten to death in the same area during protests over the island's continued division.
Turkey has some 30,000 troops stationed in northern Cyprus, which it occupied in 1974 in the wake of a short-lived Greek Cypriot coup engineered by the military ruling Greece at the time.
The former commander of Turkish forces in the north, General Hasan Kundakci, ended his tour of duty one day after Solomos's killing.
The other four accused are in the Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus, which is recognised only by Turkey.
Kenan Akin, agriculture minister of the breakaway state, appointed shortly after the death of the Greek Cypriot, has denied the accusations.
"I was not even there at the time when the shooting took place," he told Reuters last month.
Cypriot authorities claim to have photographic and video evidence of the suspects involvement in the killing.
"Their portraits are very clear," Markides said.
